sentences.text: Camp is, I suppose, all right; the food is not to be borne, and the friend who shares my cabin snores beyond all reason.
Yesterday we went upon the water in a narrow boat, which I overturned; and the whole party was diverted, to my own very considerable mortification.
There is, however, a girl of the name of Kayla, who is really fine company; she is from Ohio, and knows a great deal of horses.
We walk down to the lake after dinner, and talk of nothing in particular; I think she likes me, though I am not certain of it, which is the usual condition of such discoveries.
Will you send me more refreshments? and the device which keeps me within your call, which I have entirely forgotten.
The persons set over us are not a little strict, though in general tolerable.
P.S. I beg you will not let Max use my room.

notes.before: Yesterday we went canoeing and I flipped the canoe and everybody laughed.
notes.after: Yesterday we went upon the water in a narrow boat, which I overturned; and the whole party was diverted, to my own very considerable mortification.

notes.before: The counselors are kind of strict but mostly fine.
I think she likes me but I'm not sure.
notes.after: which is the usual condition of such discoveries

explanation: Short flat sentences are joined into balanced periods with semicolons; feelings are named by judgement nouns, and modern things are rendered by what they do.
